description: We are a passionate team of 3 members from Chattogram participating in the NASA Space Apps Challenge and our team is already complete and fully ready to build. We love coding, web technologies and turning open NASA data into clean, working prototypes for both local and global judging. Excited to take on this challenge, work hard together and bring our project to life!
summary: We developed Astraea, an autonomous, offline spacesuit wrist cuff HUD and cabin telemetry monitoring system engineered to NASA STD 3001 human system standards. Astraea addresses the challenge of astronaut self assessment during long duration missions where Earth communication delays can reach up to 20 minutes. By continuously tracking Crew Heart Rate, Blood Oxygen Saturation (SpO₂), Suit Internal Pressure and Partial Pressure CO₂ (ppCO₂) in real time, Astraea's onboard decision engine automatically diagnoses acute medical emergencies such as hypercapnia, hypobaric decompression and EVA metabolic strain and activates life support countermeasures within two seconds without waiting for ground control. This capability is critical for future Artemis lunar operations and Mars expeditions, empowering astronauts with zero latency clinical autonomy, clear color coded visual alerts and an offline Mission BlackBox flight recorder to prevent life threatening conditions in deep space.
details:
When Earth is 20 minutes away, Astraea acts in two seconds.

Astraea is a lightweight, offline autonomous health monitoring system built for an astronaut's spacesuit wrist cuff display (EVA HUD) or spacecraft workstation. It protects crew members during emergencies without waiting for instructions from Earth.

What It Does and How It Works:

1. Live Vital Sign and Cabin Tracking:
Astraea monitors four critical metrics in real time: Heart Rate (BPM), Blood Oxygen Saturation (SpO2 %), Suit Internal Pressure (kPa) and Partial Pressure CO2 (mmHg). Smooth live graphs and bright numeric readouts let astronauts check their status at a single glance.

2. Autonomous Clinical Evaluation:
Instead of forcing stressed astronauts to interpret raw medical numbers, Astraea checks sensor values against NASA human spaceflight safety limits. An alert banner at the top of the screen immediately explains what is happening in clear language such as Toxic Hypercapnia Risk, Hypobaric Decompression Alert or High Metabolic Exertion.

3. Automatic Life Support Response:
When a dangerous threshold is crossed, Astraea highlights the affected sensor cards in red and automatically scrolls down to the Spacesuit Life Support Actuators panel. With Auto Response turned on, the system triggers life saving hardware overrides within two seconds such as engaging Secondary LiOH Scrubber Loop 2, sealing the suit with an oxygen purge or boosting liquid cooling flow.

4. Offline Mission BlackBox and Simulator:
Every telemetry reading is saved locally to an offline Mission BlackBox so flight surgeons can review and export flight logs later. A built in Telemetry Simulator also lets crews and judges test normal flight conditions alongside simulated emergencies.

Key Benefits:

1. Instant Crew Protection: Acts within two seconds during deep space missions when Earth communication is delayed.

2. Lower Cognitive Load: Replaces confusing raw telemetry with clear diagnoses and automated countermeasures.

3. Complete Offline Reliability: Runs locally inside a spacesuit or habitat with zero internet or backend dependency.

Intended Impact:

As human exploration moves beyond Earth orbit toward the Moon and Mars, astronauts need smart onboard tools to handle medical emergencies independently. Astraea turns passive spacesuit sensors into an active health officer that keeps crews safe anywhere in deep space.

Tools, Coding Languages and Software Used:

1. Web Technologies: HTML5, CSS3 and JavaScript

2. Live Telemetry Charts: Chart.js for smooth real time waveform rendering

3. Offline Storage: Browser LocalStorage and JSON file export for the Mission BlackBox

4. Design and Typography: Google Fonts (Poppins) with a dark cosmic HUD theme

Creativity and Innovation:

Most health monitors only display numbers and wait for human action. Astraea closes the loop by pairing clinical diagnosis with automatic viewport scrolling and two second hardware actuation, acting as a true autonomous health officer on the astronaut's wrist.

Factors Our Team Considered:

1. Pressurized Suit Usability: Removed manual keyboard typing during emergencies so everything works through automated sensors and single tap controls.

2. Preventing Alert Fatigue: Replaced constant, distracting alarm beeps with a calm, high contrast visual interface that draws attention only when needed.

3. Helmet Visor Clarity: Designed a dark midnight color palette with glowing cyan and red borders to prevent glare inside a spacesuit visor.

Use of Super Intelligence (SI):

We used AI tools to accelerate brainstorming, interface structure and documentation.

Google Gemini: Used for brainstorming project ideas, refining UX copy, structuring documentation and assisting with frontend code logic (all reviewed, tested and edited by our team).

No NASA logos or official branding were used in any AI generated outputs.

AI helped speed up our workflow, while all system design, clinical logic and final execution were led by Team Victorious.
